title: Root-to-Leaf Path Hits the Target
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree of integers and a number target. Return true if some path that starts at the root and ends at a leaf has node values adding up to exactly target, and false otherwise.

A leaf is a node with no children. An empty tree has no paths, so the answer for it is always false.

examples.why: The root alone sums to 1, but it has a child, so it is not a leaf. The only path is 1 + 2 = 3.
Values and target can be negative, so you cannot stop early once the sum passes the target.

hints: Instead of tracking the sum so far, track what is still missing.
Going into a child, subtract the current node's value from the target. What must be true at a leaf?
Recurse: at null return false; at a leaf return target === node.val; otherwise ask either child with target − node.val.

explain.intuition:
Each step down the tree uses up part of the target. So pass the remaining amount down: a child is asked for target − node.val. At a leaf the question becomes trivial: is the remaining amount exactly the leaf's value?

The check must happen at leaves, not at null pointers. If you check at null, a node with one child looks like a path end, and [1, 2] with target 1 would wrongly return true.
steps: If root is a leaf, return root.val === target.
pitfalls: Returning true when the remaining target hits 0 at a null child. A one-child node is not a leaf.
Pruning once the running sum exceeds the target. With negative values a later node can bring it back down.
Returning true for an empty tree with target 0. There is no path at all.

solutions.title: Recursive DFS on the remaining target
solutions.idea: Subtract each node's value on the way down and test for equality at the leaves.

solutions.title: Iterative stack of (node, sum so far)
solutions.idea: Avoid recursion: push each node with the sum of the path that reaches it and check the sum when you pop a leaf.

followups: Return every root-to-leaf path that hits the target, not just whether one exists.
Count paths that hit the target when a path may start and end at any node, as long as it goes downward. (Hint: prefix sums in a hash map.)
